tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final configuration on any peg must be a descending stack: larger disks at the bottom, smaller disks on top, with no larger disk above a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When checking whether the goal state is valid or after constructing a move list to verify the final arrangement.
tower-of-hanoi.example: A goal peg listed as [5,4,3,2,1] from bottom to top is valid; any order like [5,3,4,2,1] violates the rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free Blocked Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk that has any smaller disks stacked above it cannot be moved; those smaller disks must be relocated first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Disk 3 on a peg cannot be moved while disk 1 sits on top; move disk 1 elsewhere first.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: In a three‑peg problem, the peg that is neither the source nor the destination can be used as a temporary holding area for disks while you rearrange the source or destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to clear a peg or hold disks temporarily during a sub‑move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: While moving disk 3 from peg 1 to peg 2, use peg 0 to store disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must take the topmost disk from the source peg and place it onto a destination peg whose current top disk (or empty state) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing any move, verify these two conditions.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 onto a peg whose top is disk 1 is illegal because 2 > 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing a move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to ensure every move is legal and that the final arrangement matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: As a final verification step before outputting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Step through the 7‑move sequence and confirm the final peg 2 stack is [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The output format expects peg identifiers 0, 1, 2; using any other numbering (e.g., 1‑based) will cause the verifier to reject the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the move list, always label pegs with 0‑based indices.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Use [1,2,0] to move disk 1 from peg 2 to peg 0, not [1,3,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep an up‑to‑date record of the topmost disk on every peg after each move, so you know which disks are movable and which destination pegs are legal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Throughout the planning and execution of the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 1 to peg 0, peg 0’s top becomes 1 and peg 2’s top becomes 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Leverage Existing Larger Disks on Target as Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg already contains larger disks that are correctly placed, you can place a smaller disk directly onto that peg without moving the larger ones.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has a correctly ordered stack of larger disks and you need to add a smaller disk on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Peg 2 already has [5,4]; after clearing smaller disks, you can place disk 3 onto it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Destination Peg of Smaller Top Disk Before Placing Larger Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg’s top disk is smaller than the disk you intend to move, you must first relocate the smaller top disk(s) elsewhere before placing the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk needs to be moved onto a peg whose current top is smaller.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 3 onto peg 2 whose top is disk 1, first move disks 1 and 2 to other pegs.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Smallest Disk as Flexible Buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating ordering, making it an ideal temporary buffer for shuffling other disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary holding spot that will never block larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free up a larger disk underneath.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving the desired disk without checking the destination’s top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the moving disk’s size with the destination’s top disk (or empty) before committing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook the stack order and assume any disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Track the top disk on each peg; only that disk may be moved.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may aim to finish quickly and ignore the required final ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Verify that the goal peg already contains the correct larger base before adding smaller disks, or postpone adding small disks until the larger ones are settled.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Habit from other contexts where pegs are numbered from 1.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Explicitly label pegs as 0, 1, 2 in the move list and double‑check the indices.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the constructed moves are correct without testing them.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After writing the move list, simulate each move from the initial state and compare the resulting configuration to the goal before submitting.
